consensus_summary: Milk primarily symbolizes elementary/basic spiritual teaching or nourishment for new or immature believers (positive craving of pure word for growth; corrective mark of stunted maturity), contrasted with solid food for the mature; OT milk-and-honey abundance is a distinct alternative.
book_summary: Milk is the word received—teaching another has already digested, swallowed without work; the right first food of babes, given to grow them and meant to be outgrown at weaning. Churned, it becomes butter—the word worked toward solid food.
consensus_core_identification: elementary spiritual teaching/nourishment for immature believers (vs. solid food)
book_core_identification: pre-digested received teaching (swallowed without work) as first food of babes to be outgrown; churned into butter as worked word toward solid food
boundary_disagreement: Book restricts milk to teaching already digested by another and received without the learner's work, plus an obligatory temporary/weaning status and a churning process that turns it into butter as intermediate to solid food; consensus treats elementary doctrine more broadly without those preconditions or the butter transformation.
rationale: Minimum cores both center on milk as elementary nourishment/teaching for spiritual babes drawn from the same NT texts (1 Cor 3, Heb 5, 1 Pet 2) and weaning motif (Isa 28). The book therefore preserves the consensus referent/category. It materially narrows conditions and precision, however, by defining the teaching as already digested by another and effortless to swallow, and by extending the image via Prov 30:33 churning into butter (linked also to Isa 7:15) as the worked stage toward solid food. This is boundary/precision refinement (BOOK_NARROWS + BOOK_SUBSET), not mere wording (MATCH), not core replacement (DIVERGENT), and not an uncovered referent (NOVEL).
strongest_objection: The 'already digested by another / swallowed without work' gloss and the milk-to-butter-to-solid-food progression are interpretive additions not required by the cited verses or the consensus, which treat milk more simply as basic doctrine or pure word.
